subject: Finding change points in linear trends with INLA, segmented regression

messages.author: 34e0c5cc388f8ce9
messages.subject: Finding change points in linear trends with INLA, segmented regression
parts:
Hi there,

I am analyzing trends in annual cancer rates, which is looking for multiple break points in the rates over time. Traditionally, cancer epidemiologists would use JoinPoint regression program but I've seen this carried out in the R package segmented (frequentist) and have been pointed to the mcp (Bayesian) R package. I'm wondering if this functionality could be replicated in INLA. 

E.g. we have annual trends over time, we would want to find the break points over time and we can specify how many breakpoints the model should be looking for (where # of breakpoints could be 1, 2, or 3 break points).

I can get example data if that helps. Any thoughts would be appreciated!

Thanks!

Jonathan

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Finding change points in linear trends with INLA, segmented regression
parts:
you can not estimate the changepoints in INLA, but you can can condition
on them, then use INLA to compute the marginal likelihood, hence you you
know the posterior for that changepoint up to a normalizing constant.

Variants of this was done in

author = {J. Wyse and N. Friel and H. Rue},
title = {Approximate simulation-free {B}ayesian inference for
multiple changepoint models with dependence within
segments (with discussion)},
journal = {Bayesian Analysis},
keywords = {year2011,


Best
H
